results.summary_before: This project implements a 64-byte RAM using latch-based storage, with an 8-bit data bus and 6-bit address bus. Writes take two cycles and only one write can be in flight at a time to avoid glitches and ensure data stability. The design was tested on silicon and confirmed working by the author, who noted the need to work around potential contention on an internal tristate bus. It provides a simple memory block for small data storage in digital systems.

results.summary_before: This project implements an Alternating Step Generator (ASG) using three linear feedback shift registers (LFSRs) to produce a pseudo-random bit sequence with an extremely long period. The design is a naive implementation generated with SpinalHDL, and it requires loading non-null seeds into the three LFSRs via the loadIt input before enabling operation. A new random bit is generated every clock cycle. The ASG is notable for its simple hardware implementation and huge period, making it suitable for cryptographic or simulation applications.

The design is a naive implementation, with the provided Verilog generated using SpinalHDL, and it requires loading non-null seeds into the three LFSRs via the loadIt input before enabling operation. A new random bit is generated every clock cycle. The ASG is notable for its simple hardware implementation and huge period, which the author presents as a hardware implementation example.

results.summary_before: This design implements a digital clock that generates a one-second pulse to increment seconds, minutes, and hours, which are then decoded and displayed on a 7-segment display. It requires an external 7-segment display and allows the user to select from several input clock frequencies (10, 12, 14, or 20 MHz) via switches. The clock also provides inputs to show minutes or hours, likely for setting or testing purposes. The project is a straightforward ASIC desktop clock with minimal external hardware needs.

It is tested by applying a time-varying input to the Vin terminal, connecting a threshold voltage to Vth, and observing the rate-encoded output at the Out terminal. External hardware required includes a function generator, oscilloscope, and multimeter. The design is a single-node neuron component with minimal documentation beyond its basic function.

results.summary_before: This design implements the Izhikevich spiking neuron model in digital hardware with configurable A and B parameters and selectable neuron modes. It accepts a 5-bit input current and outputs an 8-bit signed membrane potential, with parameters set via input pins. The design is verified using a cocotb testbench that sweeps modes, parameters, and input currents. External hardware is required to drive the inputs and read the output, making it suitable for neuromorphic computing experiments.

results.summary_before: This is an 8-bit single-cycle CPU based on Ramyad Hadidi's 'CPU In a Week' design, extended with CLR and MUL instructions. It includes a register file and an ALU, and supports basic ALU operations, load/store, and status checks, but lacks a program counter and external memory. The processor is tested through 12 testbenches covering basic functionality, though timing interactions are not fully verified. It is purely a simulation model with no external hardware interface.
